Scope addition (seat call), from PR #32741's contract delta review at `533a4f93` (should-fix S4, carried here instead of another PR round): with holder B disabled, the read-side hydrator lays a package-less `email_template` row into the bare slot under A's envelope, and re-enabling B does not re-hydrate. The protocol's exact read stays safe (the stored row answers first, 409 naming both), but the registry's `getPackageScopedItem(type, name, A)` serves that bare-slot entry as A's own, so the send's read and the scoped list's registry half answer the environment body as A's until the next unscoped hydration. From reading, not measured; not a regression (main always laid the row into the first holder's slot). When this card resumes: assert the slot after re-enable (as the two-holder CONTROL does), and heal on enable if it shows the copy.

Measured for the scope note 6835680498 (contract review S4 on #32741, head `533a4f9328f0800da22536a90c5b07d7b256a768`): in the `[#32568 × #32497]` pin of `packages/objectql/src/package-scoped-exact-qualifier.test.ts` (two holders A and B, B disabled, one unscoped list read to run the read-side hydrator, then B re-enabled), `registry.getPackageScopedItem(type, name, A)` after the re-enable answers:

- `email_template`: the environment's body under A's envelope (`label: 'env en-US'`, `_packageId: 'com.acme.alpha'`, `_provenance: 'package'`); B's slot answers B's own (`beta en-US`).
- `action`, `queue`: each slot answers its holder's own item (the sealed row is declined, not registered).

The protocol's exact reads in the same state answer 409 naming both for `email_template` (pinned there). The slot is re-registered only by the next unscoped hydration; enabling a package runs none.

Related cell from PR #32802 (card #32791) · 2026-11-12T22:51Z — the epic seat files it in this card's family, not as a must-fix of PR #32802.

Composition: one `sys_metadata` row of an `action` name with no package, read by a `DatabaseLoader`; one package (ALPHA) registers its item of the same name in memory **after** the boot priming pass; no second holder. A read naming no package (`MetadataManager.get` / `getDiagnosed`) answers by which package the host declares:

- host declares no package, or ALPHA: the in-memory item (older than PR #32802; not moved by it);
- host declares another package: the package-less row (PR #32802's table, row 5, declared and pinned).

One holder in every case, so no ambiguity is answered by order (red line 2 holds). The two answers differ only in whether the in-memory item or the stored package-less copy wins at one holder's name, which is this card's question for sealed types. When this card is worked, measure this `action` cell beside its own and decide whether the same rule settles both. Sources: PR #32802's contract review r2 (6837557059, N9) and the epic red-line delta read on PR #32802.
